patch_list: Block tracking

Stops the usage analytics the app sends to Wikimedia (Event Platform and Test Kitchen events about what you tap, read and search, and how long you use the app) and the Google Play install referrer. The app has no setting for this. Reading,…
Don't send install ID

Stops sending the app's permanent install ID (the X-WMF-UUID header) with every request to Wikipedia, which lets all your reading and searching on this phone be linked together, signed in or not. Block tracking doesn't cover it. Links to d…
Hide Donate buttons
Hides the Donate entry in the More menu. Off by default: it is only there for when you want to donate, and Hide donation requests already stops the prompts.
Hide donation requests

Hides the fundraising banners that pop up over articles, the donation reminder (its setting, the banner on top of articles and its survey) and the "You matter" donation slide in Year in Review. The Donate entry in the menu stays, so you ca…
Hide feature prompts

Stops the screens and dialogs that advertise app features by themselves: the Reading Challenge, Year in Review and "create an account" screens that open over the home screen or an article, the prompts to add the search and Reading Challeng…
Hide Games
Hides Wikipedia Games (the daily "Which came first?" game): the Games entry in the More menu, the game card on the home screen and the games module in Activity.
Hide surveys
Stops the feedback surveys that pop up by themselves: the one about the home feed and the one after using Read aloud. Feedback you send yourself still works.
Keep screen on while reading
Keeps the screen from turning off while an article is open, so it doesn't go dark while you read a long article. The screen turns off as usual elsewhere in the app.
Leave experiments

Puts you in the control group of every A/B test, so you get the app as it is for everyone and not features Wikimedia is trying out on some users (for example extra notifications about trending articles, semantic search or donation reminder…
Remove location access

Removes the location permissions, so the app can never ask for or read your location. Only Places (articles about what is near you) uses it: the map still opens and you can move it by hand, but it can't jump to where you are.
Remove unneeded permissions
Removes the Google Play install referrer, used only for install tracking, and the phone state permission, which a library adds and the app never asks for.
